verdict.rationale: PagerDuty's own Shift Agent is documented to detect calendar conflicts, find qualified replacements and coordinate schedule changes without manual intervention, which covers the coverage-request part of the story. A community comment confirms calendar overrides exist but calls them clunky, which is a usability complaint rather than a contradiction. Missing for 10: first-party docs on engineer-initiated overrides and shift swaps, any statement that non-admin responders can make these changes themselves, detail on the coverage-request flow, and hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an on-call engineer, I can take an override, swap a shift, or request coverage without an admin rebuilding the schedule

citations.quote: monitors calendars, detects potential conflicts, identifies qualified replacements, and coordinates schedule changes without manual intervention
All of them have clunky calendar overrides.
